candidate.title: BisChIP-Seq/ChIP-BS-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina image groups BisChIP-seq and ChIP-BS-seq over one chromatin-to-DNA schematic and a bisulfite/PCR inset. The left repeated cartoon is a title illustration, and the inset is a magnification, not a material split. The drawn route o1–o6 is retained and resolved as a supported Statham BisChIP-seq implementation, including further shearing of recovered ChIP DNA. ChIP-BS-seq has the same source-supported measurement purpose, but its Brinkman downstream interface is represented separately as o7–o10 so it does not inherit that unestablished additional shearing history. These member-specific interfaces are interpretations supported by primary text, not a claim that the picture depicts two experimental branches or that a sample is split. The broad pre-conversion adapter interfaces o4 and o8 are omitted visually but established by the papers. ChIP-BMS occurs only in catalogue prose and is not a separate target named by the schematic; MethylCap-BS-seq and application-specific workflows are outside scope. No identity of complete implementations, interchangeability, invention date or historical development edge is asserted.

features: Inset shows U copied as T while the methylation-associated C position remains C; the drawing also retains the methylation twig above that C after PCR.

The physical readout carrier is amplified DNA sequence. The retained twig is interpreted as indicating the original methylation state, consistent with the primary paper using cytosine base calls to determine methylation, rather than as evidence that PCR copies methyl groups.
ChIP selection provenance associates these DNA sequences with the captured chromatin feature; neither histones nor antibodies are sequenced.

The right-hand arrow ends at a blue line labeled DNA at the image edge. The primary paper establishes that the amplified adapter-bearing library is used for Illumina sequencing; no separate sequencer operation is drawn.

C-versus-T outcomes at covered cytosines support base-resolution methylation information within the enriched genomic fraction. Fragment capture limits coverage and localization of the protein association; the methylation base call is not restricted to a fragment-level resolution.
